title: Add explicit one-shot confirmation for destructive Terminal commands
goal: Allow users to explicitly approve a single destructive Terminal command without weakening Settings capability grants or persistently granting destructive access.
context: Terminal's SettingsTerminalCommandAuthorizer correctly fails closed when policy requires approval, but Terminal UI has no confirmation path. As a result, destructive commands and sync now remain unusable even when the relevant write/network grants are enabled. Approval must be one-shot and bound to the command being retried.
forbidden_changes: Do not change Settings grants or turn destructive approval into a persistent capability grant.
Do not allow confirmation to override missing read/write/network/execute grants.
Do not change GitHub sync conflict semantics or expose credentials.
Do not claim physical-device verification from CI alone.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal authorization distinguishes allowed, denied, and approval-required outcomes.
An approval-required command is not added to history or executed before confirmation.
The UI presents the exact pending command and requires explicit user confirmation.
Confirmation applies only to the immediate retry; all Settings capability grants are rechecked.
Regression test proves destructive command is blocked before confirmation and runs only when confirmation is explicitly passed.
Task-contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA gates pass.
verification: Confirm task-contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA gates.
recovery: Revert the single task commit if a command executes without confirmation or existing capability-denial behavior changes.
